observation: Dataset loaded: 384,977 rows x 22 columns
decision: Use df_raw as untouched reference; all work on df copy

observation: 384,977 rows x 22 columns; mix of numeric, binary, categorical, identifier and text fields
decision: Handle each variable type with its own preprocessing path

observation: region has 404 categories of mixed geographic granularity
decision: One-hot encoding impractical; consider grouping or target encoding fitted on train only

observation: region names are not unique locations: some names map to up to 3 Craigslist sites (e.g. jacksonville, columbus, rochester exist in multiple states)
decision: Create unique location key from region_url (or region + state); drop id, url, image_url from features

observation: Binary flags stored as integers; beds/baths are discrete
decision: Treat flags as categorical 0/1; keep beds/baths numeric

observation: price ranges from 0 to 2,768,307,249
decision: Investigate target extremes in Step 2

observation: price is extremely right-skewed: mean $8,826 vs median $1,036; max $2,768,307,249
decision: Describe rent with the median, not the mean; report robust metrics (MAE, median absolute error) alongside RMSE

observation: 1,307 listings at $0 and 731 at $1 (2,214 below $100 in total); examples are real apartments with no price entered
evidence: 2.2 threshold counts, 2.3 repeated values, 2.4 example listings
decision: Placeholders, not rents: remove rows with price < $100 before the train/test split

observation: 269 listings above $10,000: a mix of genuine luxury homes (large houses in LA, Seattle, SF Bay), sale prices of homes posted as rentals, and nonsense values
evidence: 2.2 threshold counts, 2.4 example listings, 2.5 full-range histogram
decision: Remove rows with price > $10,000; state in the report that the system is scoped to rents up to $10,000 (too few luxury rows for a model to learn from)

observation: Some listings are properties for SALE posted in the rental section (e.g. manufactured homes 'for sale' with a separate lot rent)
decision: In Step 5, search descriptions for sale wording, since cheaper sale listings may sit inside the valid range

observation: The same absurd price $679,710 appears 30 times, all from one complex (jacksonville, NC)
decision: Evidence of one listing reposted many times; quantify duplicates in Step 4

observation: Plausibility rule $100-$10,000 removes 2,483 rows (0.64%)
decision: Fixed domain rule (not learned from data), so applying it before the split does not cause leakage

observation: Log transform alone does not fix the target: log skew is -5.14 before filtering (pulled by $0/$1) vs 0.31 after; raw skew of valid prices is 2.84
decision: Filter invalid prices first, then model log1p(price); convert predictions back with expm1

observation: Q-Q plot: log prices follow a normal shape except a heavier lower tail (rents of roughly $100-$250)
decision: Re-examine very low rents with price per sqft in Step 5 (possible rooms, shared units or weekly rates)

observation: Log-price deciles hold 9.1%-10.9% of valid listings each; unevenness comes from popular round prices (e.g. $950, $1,000)
evidence: 2.8 decile table, spiky log1p histogram in 2.7
decision: Stratify the train/test split on log-price deciles (Step 7)

observation: Gaps in 4 fields only: parking 36.5%, laundry 20.5%, lat/long 0.50%, description 2 rows
decision: Each field gets its own strategy (3.5-3.7); all other columns are complete

observation: Parking is missing in 91% of rows where laundry is missing vs 23% where laundry is present; lat and long always missing together
decision: Gaps are linked (poster effort), not independent random failures: not MCAR

observation: Parking-missing rate ranges from 7% to 65% across states
evidence: 3.2 matrix sorted by state, 3.4 missing rate by state and type
decision: Missingness depends on location (MAR); location features help the model account for it

observation: Blank parking: median rent $1,020 vs $1,057 when present (-3.5%), a small rent difference; within-state median gap -0.7%, same direction in 28 of 49 states
evidence: 3.5 median comparison, category chart, within-state check
decision: Keep blank parking as its own 'missing' category (separate from the explicit 'no' category); never fill with the most common value

observation: Blank laundry: median rent $1,010 vs $1,050 when present (-3.8%), a small rent difference; within-state median gap -2.4%, same direction in 33 of 49 states
evidence: 3.5 median comparison, category chart, within-state check
decision: Keep blank laundry as its own 'missing' category (separate from the explicit 'no' category); never fill with the most common value

observation: Filling blank parking with the most common value ('off-street parking', median $936) would put 139,796 listings with median $1,020 into a group -8% away from their actual rent level
decision: Confirms mode imputation would mislabel these listings; use a separate 'missing' category

observation: Filling blank laundry with the most common value ('w/d in unit', median $1,299) would put 78,667 listings with median $1,010 into a group +29% away from their actual rent level
decision: Confirms mode imputation would mislabel these listings; use a separate 'missing' category

observation: 1,918 listings lack coordinates; region_url and state are always known for them
decision: Fill lat/long with the median coordinates of the listing's region_url, learned on training data only; regions with too few located listings fall back to the state median; invalid coordinates from Step 5 get the same treatment

observation: 2 listings have no description
decision: No action: description is not a model feature (used only for duplicate and leakage checks)

observation: No exact duplicate rows (0); every id is unique
decision: Exact-duplicate removal alone would miss the problem; check looser levels

observation: 46,544 extra copies (12.09%) are reposts: identical except id and url; largest group has 141 copies
decision: Remove reposts before the train/test split

observation: 191,384 extra copies (49.71%) are identical to the model (same features and price); 5,006 groups have 10+ copies
decision: Deduplicate on model features + price, keeping one row per group (also removes all reposts)

observation: Without deduplication, 58.9% of test rows have an identical twin in training (simulated 80/20 split); 51.6% after removing reposts; 0.0% after level-4 deduplication
decision: Deduplicate BEFORE splitting to prevent leakage and an over-optimistic test score

observation: 203,909 listings reuse a photo from another listing
decision: Evidence only: different real units can share a building photo, so photo alone is not a deletion rule

observation: Cleaning order matters: fixing values can create new identical rows
decision: Step 7 order: price rule -> validity fixes (Step 5) -> deduplication -> stratified split

observation: Level-4 deduplication removes 50% of valid rows: 382,494 become 192,470
decision: Still ample for all five models; from Step 6 on, EDA of relationships uses valid, deduplicated rows so large complexes with hundreds of copies don't dominate the charts

observation: sqfeet: 48 zeros and 1 at the 2^23-1 placeholder; outside 100-10,000 sq ft: 1,058 listings (1,034 in the valid price range)
evidence: 5.1 quantiles, threshold counts, repeated values, examples
decision: Remove rows with sqfeet outside 100-10,000 (0 means 'not entered'; size is a core user input)

observation: beds up to 1,100; above 8: 4 listings (4 in the valid price range); 0 beds = studio (valid)
decision: Remove rows with beds > 8

observation: baths up to 75; above 8: 5 listings (4 in the valid price range); 3,107 listings with 0 baths; half-baths normal
decision: Remove rows with baths > 8; keep 0 baths (shared-bathroom units) and half-baths

observation: Under 70 sq ft per room (sqfeet / (beds + 1)): 122 listings (121 in the valid price range); baths > beds + 3: 32 listings (32 in the valid price range)
decision: Remove physically impossible size/room combinations; baths > beds + 3 kept as a warning only

observation: Coordinates outside the U.S.: 262 listings (262 in the valid price range); more than 500 km from their region centre: 827 listings (814 in the valid price range)
decision: Set these coordinates to missing and use the Step 3 regional fill; region centres from training data only

observation: Each Craigslist site has 2 state label(s) at most; e.g. the Reno site is labelled 'ca' although Reno is in Nevada
decision: Interpret state as 'state of the Craigslist site'; exact location comes from region_url and coordinates

observation: Strong sale wording ('for sale', down payment, sale/asking price, owner financing): 1,794 listings (1,691 in the valid price range)
evidence: 5.8 pattern table and matches in context
decision: Remove listings with strong sale wording (not monthly rents); 'rent to own' is kept as a rental

observation: 694 listings priced $100-$249; 501 of them mention weekly pricing
evidence: 5.9 wording comparison, price per sq ft, examples
decision: Remove weekly-priced listings under $250 (price is not monthly); other cheap listings kept

observation: Estimated modelling dataset: 384,977 raw -> 382,494 after price rule -> 379,158 after validity rules -> 190,221 after deduplication
decision: Order in Step 7: price rule -> validity rules (coordinates blanked) -> deduplication -> stratified split
